To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“high life expectancy in a country is caused by a combination of high level of country wealth and governance, high level of education and health system, and low income inequality.”.
high life expectancy in a country can be achieved by the configuration of high level of wealth, education, governance, and health system.
the configurations of the five structural conditions are usually sufficient for high or low life expectancies in different countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the configurational effects and the complex fusion of policies on health.
a new approach for studying the effects of structural conditions on health and provides a new perspective to the field of health equity research.
the configuration of the structural determinants of health and their causal effects on life expectancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the configuration of the structural determinants of health can be considered a sufficient condition for life expectancy.
high life expectancy is usually caused by a configuration of conditions that includes high levels of governance, education wealth and an affluent health system.
the CSDH was right in emphasizing the importance of a complex fusion of actions in the pursuit of health equity and well-being.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CSDH recommendations should be taken seriously.
the configuration of the structural determinants of health is important for health.

the more countries invest in their health systems and in the quality of governance, and the more they reduce the level of inequality and increase the level of education, the better their health will be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CSDH approach is not only a good way of thinking about the complex interrelations among the different sectors, but it also provides an effective way to analyze and explain health outcomes.
a set-theoretic approach can be a valuable tool for exploring the complex causal relations between different conditions and health.
the configuration of conditions, not the individual effects of each condition, is important for understanding the causal complexity of life expectancy.
